suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read without optional chaining. WHY: when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (the new default for many callers), the destructured value is undefined and the Google Meet fallback throws a TypeError, which breaks booking creation. HOW: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the fallback in updateEvent and deleteEvent runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, and it then calls `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, which compares against that same falsy value. WHY: the find never matches, so the fallback always yields undefined instead of the destination calendar's externalId, which is a regression from the previous behaviour. HOW: fall back to `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: createEvent now takes a required `credentialId` and picks the calendar by matching credentialId. WHY: destination calendars that have no credentialId (the integration-only branch in EventManager) never match, so the event goes to 'primary' instead of the selected calendar. The other implementations (Office365, Lark, CalDAV) ignore the new argument, so the interface change is inconsistent. HOW: fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId when no credentialId matches.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` is a no-op when destinationCalendar is null. WHY: the evt is built with null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, so a collective event silently drops all team members' destination calendars. Separately, teamDestinationCalendars is filled inside async map callbacks, which is fragile.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In updateEvent and deleteEvent, the fallback runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy. It then calls `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing against that same falsy value. This almost never matches, so the fallback always yields undefined. Before this change it returned destinationCalendar.externalId. Use the first destination calendar instead, for example `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`, or match on credentialId.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined when destinationCalendar is null or empty. Many handlers now set it to [] and handleNewBooking can set it to null. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for a Google Meet location. The original code used `?.`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, because the destructured value is undefined. Several call sites now pass `[]`. Use optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and it looks for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. That comparison can never match, so the result is always undefined. The same pattern appears in deleteEvent at lines 315-317. Fall back to the first destination calendar's externalId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` when `evt.destinationCalendar` is null or an empty array. Both are now produced, for example by handleNewBooking when there is no calendar and by the `[]` fallbacks in other handlers. `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` then throws a TypeError for a Google Meet location. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the fallback branch `externalCalendarId` is falsy. `find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` therefore compares against undefined, null or an empty string, and almost never matches. The destination-calendar fallback is now dead in both updateEvent (line 256) and deleteEvent (line 317). Fall back to the first destination calendar instead: `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `evt.destinationCalendar` can be `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` then does nothing, so a collective event drops all team members' calendars even when they have them. Initialize it to `[]` and push into that, or build the array in one step.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `destinationCalendar` is now an array that handleNewBooking, and the other handlers, can set to null or []. Destructuring `[mainHostDestinationCalendar]` then yields undefined, and `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking where the user has no destination calendar. The previous code used `?.`. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Use optional chaining: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: In the fallback branch use the first destination calendar's externalId, e.g. `event.destinationCalendar?.[0]?.externalId`. Do not search by `externalCalendarId`, which is falsy in that branch.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. WHY: a team admin who is not also an owner is denied, so the permission check is wrong. Separately, any attendee matched by email can add guests, which is a looser permission than the organizer/admin model. HOW: use || between the two team checks, and consider limiting attendee access.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the dedupe and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive. The blacklist is lowercased but the guest is not, and the existing-attendee check compares raw strings. WHY: Foo@x.com bypasses the blacklist and duplicates an existing foo@x.com attendee. Duplicates inside the submitted list are also not removed server-side. HOW: lowercase each guest before comparing, and dedupe the list.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) receives the raw input guests instead of the filtered uniqueGuests. WHY: blacklisted or duplicate guests are treated as new and get the 'scheduled' email, and existing attendees whose email is in the input also get that email. Also, updateCalendarAttendees is not wrapped in error handling, so a calendar failure happens after the DB write and leaves the attendees added but the request returning an error. HOW: pass uniqueGuests and handle calendar errors.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist is lowercased but the guest email is not, so the check is bypassed by changing case (e.g. 'Blocked@Example.com'). The attendee dedupe has the same problem. Normalize both sides: compare guest.toLowerCase() against the lowercased, trimmed blacklist entries, and compare attendee.email.toLowerCase() in the dedupe filter. Also lowercase the isAttendee comparison at line 52 (attendee.email.toLowerCase() === user.email.toLowerCase()).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The handler computes `uniqueGuests` (existing attendees and blacklisted emails removed) but passes the raw `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails. Any submitted email that was filtered out, such as an existing attendee or a blacklisted address, is still in `newGuests`. If it matches an attendee, that attendee gets the 'scheduled' email instead of the 'guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with &&. Only a user who passes both checks is authorized through this path, so team admins who are not owners are wrongly rejected. The variable name and intent call for ||.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but the guest email is compared without lowercasing. A blacklisted address submitted in mixed case, such as Foo@x.com, bypasses the blacklist. Compare `guest.toLowerCase()`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The subject uses `attendees[0].name`, which assumes the original booker is first in the list. The attendee list comes from a prisma include with no orderBy, and new guests are created with name "". If a new guest ends up at index 0, the subject has an empty name. Order the attendees explicitly, or take the name from the original booking's first attendee.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Server-side uniqueness is not enforced within the input list: duplicate emails in `guests` all pass the filter and createMany inserts duplicate attendees (only the client dialog checks uniqueness). The blacklist check is also case-sensitive (guest is not lowercased). Normalize the guests to lowercase and dedupe with a Set before filtering. Also pass uniqueGuests, not guests, to sendAddGuestsEmails.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The attendees are committed to the DB before eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees runs, and that call is not wrapped in try/catch. If it throws, the user sees an error but the guests are already persisted and the calendar event is not updated. A retry then fails with emails_must_be_unique_valid. Handle the failure (catch and log or compensate), or do the calendar update before the persist, or make the two steps atomic.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isTeamAdminOrOwner uses && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so it is only true for users who pass both checks. Team admins who are not owners are wrongly denied. Use ||.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error toast is built as `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`. That string is always truthy, so the `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` fallback can never run, and the unable_to_add_guests key added in common.json is dead. Users also see a raw tRPC code such as 'BAD_REQUEST: ...'. Show only the translated message, and fall back to unable_to_add_guests when the message is empty.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isTeamAdminOrOwner combines the two checks with &&, so it means 'admin AND owner' while the name says 'admin OR owner'. Use || so the name and the behaviour match. Separately, the FORBIDDEN message 'you_do_not_have_permission' was not found in en/common.json, so the dialog toast may show the raw key.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}), not the parsed key. The result is written directly as `key` in prisma.credential.update. WHY: the credential key is overwritten with {success:true,data:{...}}, which breaks all later Google auth parsing for that credential. HOW: use `.data` of the parsed result, after checking `.success`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: in sync mode the function returns the raw fetch Response, but callers expect the shape of their normal refresh function. Google reads `res?.data`, and axios-based callers (zoho-bigin, zohocrm) read `.data.error`. WHY: a fetch Response has no `.data`, so these callers throw or misbehave whenever credential sync is enabled. HOW: normalize the return value, for example by parsing the JSON and wrapping it in the expected shape. Also add a content-type header, a timeout, and an `ok` check on the response.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure, so `tokenResponse.success` is always true by the time it is read. The previous non-throwing behaviour and the error logging were removed. WHY: a malformed refresh response now throws instead of being tolerated, which is a regression.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: a direct token refresh was added in the connection getter. It runs on every connection, with no expiry check and no refreshOAuthTokens wrapper. WHY: it adds an extra network call to every use of the service and ignores credential sync. The `.success` check on parseRefreshTokenResponse is redundant because that function throws on failure. The refresh also does not use the sync endpoint.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time. A header value that is an array also passes through this comparison unchecked. The code also calls zod `.parse`, JSON.parse and symmetricDecrypt without try/catch, and it never validates that the decrypted keys are an object. WHY: invalid input produces a 500 instead of a 4xx, and the non-constant-time compare may allow timing attacks. HOW: use crypto.timingSafeEqual and wrap the parsing and decryption in try/catch that returns 400.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: The webhook secret is compared with !==, which leaks timing information. Use crypto.timingSafeEqual on equal-length buffers. Also handle array-valued headers and reject a missing header explicitly. This endpoint can write arbitrary credentials for any userId, so a leaked secret is high impact.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is `userId` and is sent to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`. This call passes `credentialId`, so the name and the value disagree. When credential sync is enabled, the endpoint receives a credential id as a user id. Pass the credential's userId (credential.userId) instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comments say "any property with a number is the expiry" and "allow other properties". The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` evaluate to a fixed string like "ZodString", so the schema does not do either. It requires a literal key and does not match any numeric property. Use `.passthrough()` and an explicit expiry field, or fix the comments to match what the schema does.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod safeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credentials. The old code stored the output of googleCredentialSchema.parse(...). Now `key` is the wrapper object, so the credential row is saved as {success:true,data:{...}} and later reads of access_token/refresh_token break. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` as the key. Also, when credential sync is enabled refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens's third parameter is userId, but credentialId is passed. With credential sync enabled this sends a credential id as calcomUserId, so the sync endpoint refreshes the wrong user's tokens, or none. Pass the credential's userId. Also, in sync mode the helper returns a fetch Response, while this code reads tokenInfo.data (an axios shape), so it breaks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType ({success, data}), not the parsed data. Assigning it to `key` and saving it to prisma stores `{success, data}` as the credential key, which breaks the Google credentials. Use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data`. Also, when credential sync is on, refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` evaluate to fixed strings such as '[object Object]'. They are not wildcard keys. The schema therefore requires a literal bogus numeric property and always fails, so sync mode always throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. The schema should use passthrough with an optional expiry. Also, `refresh_token` is overwritten with the literal string 'refresh_token' whenever it is missing, and that placeholder gets persisted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The third parameter of refreshOAuthTokens is userId, but `credentialId` is passed. Credential sync would then send a credential id as calcomUserId to the sync endpoint. Pass the credential's userId instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns the zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), not the parsed credentials. It is assigned to `key` and written to prisma.credential.update, so the stored Google credential becomes {success:true,data:{...}} and loses its top-level access_token and refresh_token. Every later refresh and API call then breaks. Use `.data` from the result. Also, parseRefreshTokenResponse is given the already-merged googleCredentials rather than the refresh response, so in sync mode it validates the wrong object.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Two problems. (1) `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` evaluates to a fixed junk key string, not 'any numeric property'. The minimum schema therefore requires a nonexistent numeric key and always fails in sync mode, so the helper throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned'. (2) `refresh_token = 'refresh_token'` is injected whenever the response lacks a refresh token. Callers that spread `data` into the stored credential (Office365 at CalendarService.ts:264, Zoom) overwrite the real refresh token with the literal placeholder. Apply the placeholder only in sync mode, and use a passthrough schema with explicit expiry handling.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens is passed `credentialId` where it expects the user id. In sync mode it POSTs calcomUserId=<credential id>, so credentials for the wrong user are fetched. In sync mode it also returns a fetch Response, but the axios-based code reads `tokenInfo.data.error`, which throws a TypeError because `data` is undefined. The same Response-versus-axios mismatch exists in the Zoho CRM and HubSpot callers. Pass the real user id, and normalise the sync response into the shape the callers expect.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParse result ({success, data}), but it is used here as the credential key. Before this change googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the plain data. The credential's key is now saved as {success, data}, which corrupts the stored credential. Also, in credential-sync mode refreshOAuthTokens returns a fetch Response, so `res?.data` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Fix: use `.data` from the parsed result, and normalize the Response by calling .json() in sync mode.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: refreshOAuthTokens' third parameter is the cal.com userId, but this caller passes credentialId (the credential's id). With credential sync enabled, the sync endpoint is asked for the wrong user's credentials. Also, in sync mode the helper returns a fetch Response, which has no `.data`, so `tokenInfo.data.error` throws. Pass the real userId and normalize the response.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Behaviour contract change. This code used safeParse and, on failure, logged the error and continued. parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws 'Invalid refreshed tokens were returned' on failure, so refresh failures propagate and abort the caller. The error logging was also removed. Handle or catch the throw if the old tolerance is intended.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` branch of the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. The SMS cron job can therefore delete non-SMS reminders (email, WhatsApp) whose retryCount exceeds 1. Fix: put the method in an outer AND, for example `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: dayjs().toISOString() } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not guarded. If it throws, the exception escapes the catch and aborts the loop, so the remaining reminders in that cron run are skipped and the error log on the following line never runs. Fix: wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `.catch()` to log the failure and continue.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says this deletes SMS reminders whose scheduled date has passed. The new `retryCount > 1` branch of the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter and no date condition. It therefore also deletes non-SMS reminders (email, WhatsApp) that have exceeded retries, and future SMS reminders. The comment is now untrue. Either scope the branch with `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and update the comment to mention retry-exhausted reminders, or update the comment to say what is really deleted.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The SMS cron's deleteMany was previously restricted to method SMS. The new OR branch `retryCount > 1` has no method filter, so it can delete non-SMS reminders (email/WhatsApp) with retryCount > 1. Move the method condition outside the OR: `where: { method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, OR: [{ scheduledDate: { lte: ... } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } }] }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The retry-exhaustion clause `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter, unlike the first OR clause. This SMS cleanup job can therefore delete non-SMS workflow reminders (email, WhatsApp) once they have retryCount > 1. Scope it to SMS: `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The new `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` clause in the OR has no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This SMS cron job will therefore delete any WorkflowReminder, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP ones, whose retryCount is above 1. Scope it with `{ method: WorkflowMethods.SMS, retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block is not guarded. If it throws, for example because the reminder was deleted concurrently or the DB is unavailable, the exception escapes the loop. The rest of the reminders are then skipped and the handler returns a 500. Wrap the update in its own try/catch, or use `updateMany`. Also use `{ retryCount: { increment: 1 } }` instead of `reminder.retryCount + 1`, which is a stale read-then-write.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: After a successful enable call the modal moves to the DisplayBackupCodes step, and onEnable() is only called from the Close button. Dialog onOpenChange only calls the parent handler and does not reset the step or notify the parent that 2FA is now enabled. WHY: If the user dismisses the dialog by clicking the overlay or pressing Esc, 2FA is already enabled server-side but the settings UI is not refreshed through onEnable(). The step stays at DisplayBackupCodes, so reopening shows the old backup codes without the password flow. HOW: Wrap onOpenChange so that it calls resetState(), and calls onEnable() when the step is DisplayBackupCodes. Alternatively, make the dialog not dismissible on that step.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write. Two concurrent logins with the same backup code both read the same encrypted array, both find the code, and both succeed, so a 'single-use' code can be used more than once. The last writer also overwrites the other's update. Make the consume step atomic: use a transaction with row lock, or an optimistic update (updateMany where id and backupCodes equal the originally read ciphertext) and fail the login if count is 0.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The default export in BackupCode.tsx is named `TwoFactor`. It was copied from TwoFactor.tsx but renders the backup code input. This clashes with the real TwoFactor component and is misleading in stack traces and devtools. Rename it to `BackupCode`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The error log says "cannot proceed with backup code login", but this is the disable-2FA endpoint, not login. The message was copied from next-auth-options.ts. Change it to something like "cannot proceed with backup code disable".

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql, so `authConditions` is always truthy. The `else if (authConditions)` branch is only reached when filterConditions is null. The `else if (filterConditions)` and final `else` branches can never run. Simplify to: `return filterConditions ? Prisma.sql`(${authConditions}) AND (${filterConditions})` : authConditions;`

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the origin check uses `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1`, a substring match. WHY: any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl passes, and an empty origin string also matches, so a foreign window can send 'discourse-resize' messages and set the iframe height. HOW: compare for exact equality against the origin parsed from discourseUrl.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `contents << ...` mutates the caller's string in place. WHY: it raises on a frozen string and appends the footer to the caller's copy, so a caller that reuses the string gets the footer twice. HOW: use `contents = contents + ...`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the embed access check relies on the client-supplied Referer header. WHY: non-browser clients can spoof the Referer, and `embed_url` is attacker-controlled, so anyone can enqueue RetrieveTopic jobs that fetch pages from the embeddable host. HOW: do not treat the Referer as an authorization boundary.

suggestions.label: security
suggestions.suggestionContent: Origin validation uses a substring check (discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1), so any origin that is a substring of discourseUrl is accepted, such as a truncated hostname or the string 'null' if it appears in the URL. Compare for exact equality against the parsed origin of discourseUrl instead, e.g. build an anchor element or use new URL(discourseUrl).origin, then require e.origin === expectedOrigin.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: feed_key computes a 'feed-modified:<sha1>' key but nothing reads or writes it. poll_feed re-fetches and re-imports the whole feed every hour with no modified-check, so the declared key is dead code. Either use it for a conditional-fetch check or remove it.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `i.content` can be nil for feed items that carry only a description or summary. `i.content.scrub` then raises NoMethodError and aborts the whole feed import. Fall back to the description, skip items with no content, and rescue per-item errors so one bad item does not stop the loop. Example: `raw = i.content || i.description; next if raw.blank?; content = CGI.unescapeHTML(raw.scrub)`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: Check-then-create race on `embed_url`. Concurrent imports of the same URL (PollFeed running alongside RetrieveTopic) both see no embed and both create a topic. The loser raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique from `create!` on the unique index. Rescue RecordNotUnique and re-read the existing embed, or take a lock keyed on the URL.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `imported_from` link interpolates `url` into HTML (both the href attribute and the link text) without escaping. The post is stored as raw_html and rendered with `raw`, so a feed or URL containing `'`, `<` or `&` breaks the markup or injects HTML. Escape the URL (`ERB::Util.html_escape(url)`) in both places. The line also mutates the caller's `contents` string with `<<`; build a new string instead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The 'requires feed_polling_url' and 'requires embed_by_username' tests don't stub feed_polling_enabled? to true. It defaults to false, so poll_feed is never called whatever the other conditions do. Both tests pass even if the url/username checks are removed from Jobs::PollFeed#execute. Stub feed_polling_enabled? to true, plus the other two settings, in each test and blank only the one setting being tested.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `execute(...)[0]['id']` runs on an empty result when no category name matches the embed_category setting, or when that setting row is missing. `[0]` returns nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError. The same happens at line 15 if the uncategorized_category_id row is missing. WHY: this is the default case on a fresh install or a site that never set embed_category, so the migration crashes. HOW: use `row = result.first; category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0`, and guard the uncategorized lookup the same way. Also escape the host value in the INSERT, because the interpolated `'#{h}'` breaks on a quote or a blank line.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: ...).first` can return nil, and update and destroy use the result without a nil check. WHY: an unknown or already-deleted id raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a 404. HOW: use `find` or raise Discourse::NotFound. Separately, the model's before_validation calls `host.sub!` on a possibly nil host, so a request missing `embeddable_host[host]` also raises NoMethodError.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: File names and contents are swapped. embeddable_host_fabricator.rb now holds the :category, :diff_category, :happy_category and :private_category fabricators. category_fabricator.rb now holds Fabricator(:embeddable_host). Fabricators still load, but anyone looking for a fabricator by file name will look in the wrong place. Move the category fabricators back to category_fabricator.rb and keep only Fabricator(:embeddable_host) (host 'eviltrout.com', category) in embeddable_host_fabricator.rb.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The lookup compares lower(host) in the DB against uri.host, which is not lowercased. A referer with a mixed-case host, such as http://EvilTrout.com, will not match its own stored host. Normalize both sides: `host = uri.host.downcase` before the query. This fails closed rather than opening a bypass, so the impact is low.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The test 'is false if embeddable_host is blank' does not check what its name says. The topic does not stub has_topic_embed? and embed_truncate is not enabled, so expandable_first_post? is false no matter what hosts exist. Stub has_topic_embed? to true and enable embed_truncate inside this test. Then assert the result is true once a host exists, so the test shows the host state is what changes the outcome. If the host check was deliberately removed, delete the test.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration indexes `[0]` on query results without checking that any rows came back. If `embed_category` is unset (the default, so no site_settings row exists) or names no matching category, the first query returns zero rows. `[0]` is then nil and `nil['id']` raises NoMethodError, which aborts the migration. The `uncategorized_category_id` fallback query has the same problem. Use `.first`, guard for nil, and fall back, for example `row = execute(...).first; category_id = row ? row['id'].to_i : 0`.

If no `embed_category` setting row exists, which is the default, `execute(...)[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same failure happens if `uncategorized_category_id` is not in site_settings. Guard with `.first` and nil checks, or use `cmd_tuples > 0`, and fall back to the uncategorized category.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The query compares `lower(host)` against `uri.host` without downcasing it. A referer such as `http://EvilTrout.com` has `uri.host` of `EvilTrout.com` (URI may or may not normalize the case, depending on the Ruby version). It would never match the lowercased column. Use `host.downcase` in the comparison.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The migration indexes `execute(...)[0]['id']` with no nil check. If there is no `embed_category` row in site_settings, which is the default on installs that never changed it, `[0]` is nil and the migration raises NoMethodError. The same applies to the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, because that row may not exist yet. Guard both: use `.first`, check for nil, and fall back to the default category. Also, `INSERT ... '#{h}'` interpolates raw setting values, so a host containing a quote breaks the insert, and values should be stripped and escaped.

suggestions.suggestionContent: before_validation calls `self.host.sub!` with no nil check. `EmbeddableHost.new` (the create action) with a missing `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` leaves host nil, so validation raises NoMethodError and returns a 500 instead of a validation error. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...)` guarded by `host.present?`. Also, `record_for_host` compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host` without downcasing it, so mixed-case referers are rejected.

When the write now fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key stays cached for 29 minutes. Later requests from the rejected device hit the cache, return early without an error, and are authenticated as anonymous, so the device limit is bypassed after the first rejection. suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The device limit is enforced with a check-then-act sequence. CountDevices runs, then the insert runs in a separate statement with no transaction, lock or constraint. Concurrent requests from new devices can all see count < limit and all insert, so the limit is exceeded. The PR also removed the async goroutine, so requests now tag in parallel. Fix: do the count and insert atomically, for example in one transaction with a lock, or with a conditional INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE (SELECT COUNT(*) ...) < limit, or serialize through a server lock.

If tagDeviceUI fails, including with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the key stays cached, so the device is probably treated as already tagged for the cache TTL (29 minutes) and later requests are not re-evaluated. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: No double-checked cache test is done after taking the write lock, and the cache is overwritten even when the read fails. WHY: Concurrent first requests all redo the manifest read serially, and a transient error stores nil in the cache, replacing a previously valid value. HOW: After Lock(), re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`. Only assign the cache when err == nil.

suggestions.suggestionContent: After taking the write lock, re-check the cache (`if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`) so concurrent first callers do not each rebuild. Also, the assignment `entryPointAssetsCache = result` (line ~69) must only happen when err == nil. If `result` can be nil or partial on error, a failed load is stored in the cache and served to every later reader in non-dev mode. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the async legacy writes (Create at lines 50-57, Delete at 108-114, Update at 134-141, DeleteCollection at 161-167) derive their context from the request ctx via context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...). WHY: the request ctx is cancelled as soon as the handler returns, which happens right after the goroutine is started, so the legacy write is often cancelled before it completes and legacy storage silently drifts from unified storage. HOW: build a detached context for the goroutine, for example context.WithoutCancel(ctx) (Go 1.21+) or context.Background() with the logger re-attached, and apply the timeout to that.

Create (line 45) and Update (line 129) call recordLegacyDuration when the unified-storage call fails. Delete's success path (line 106) passes `name` where the other calls pass options.Kind. WHY: legacy and storage latency and error metrics are conflated and mislabeled. HOW: use recordLegacyDuration in DeleteCollection's goroutine, recordStorageDuration in the Create and Update error paths, and options.Kind in Delete.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: Delete computes the contextual `log` with name, kind and method but attaches `d.Log` to ctx (`klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`). WHY: downstream storage logs lose the name, kind and method context that the other methods propagate. HOW: use klog.NewContext(ctx, log).

Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection set up legacy expectations (or none), but nothing asserts that legacy was called, and nothing waits for the goroutine. Removing the legacy write entirely would still pass. Fix: use a shared mock, wait on a channel or use assert.Eventually, then call m.AssertCalled for the legacy method. Also, the Create error case registers its failure via setupLegacyFn on the shared mock, so it does not isolate a unified-store failure. Register the error on the storage side and assert that legacy is not called.

The same pattern is in Delete (108-114), Update (134-141) and DeleteCollection (161-167). The legacy write is then aborted or fails, so legacy storage silently diverges from unified storage. Use a detached context, e.g. context.WithTimeoutCause(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 10*time.Second, ...), and take a deep copy of obj before starting the goroutine so it does not race with the response path.

suggestions.suggestionContent: recordStorageDuration is passed `name` (the object name) where the kind label is expected; every other call passes options.Kind. This creates a high-cardinality, wrongly labelled metric. Line 97 also sets the context logger from d.Log instead of the enriched `log`.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The legacy write now runs in a goroutine, but its context is derived from the request ctx. Once the handler returns, the server cancels that ctx, so the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection calls can fail with context canceled. Legacy storage can then silently diverge from unified storage. The same pattern appears in the Update, Delete and DeleteCollection goroutines. suggestions.suggestionContent: The old Update fetched the old object and passed legacy an updateWrapper carrying the object storage had already updated. The new code passes the raw objInfo to Legacy.Update. Legacy now recomputes the update against its own stored copy, which may differ from storage. Also, the legacy error is only recorded in a metric and never logged or returned.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu during the build, and only the cache map write is locked. There is no per-key de-duplication. WHY: concurrent builds for the same NamespacedResource (for example startup init racing with getOrCreateIndex) both call bleve.New on the same directory. The second call fails with 'path already exists' for file-backed indices. For memory indices, one index overwrites the other in the cache and is leaked without being closed. HOW: serialize builds per key (a per-key mutex or singleflight), or re-check the cache under the lock before building and close any index that gets replaced.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: NewResourceServer now runs s.Init(ctx) synchronously. Previously construction was cheap and could not fail on init, and Init (lifecycle hooks, search index build, watcher start) ran separately. Construction now blocks on the full index build and returns an error if any init step fails. Callers such as apistore/restoptions.go, registry/apis/dashboard/legacy_storage.go, unified/client.go and the tests that call Init after construction (e.g. watcher_test.go:148) were not updated for this. A transient backend or lifecycle failure at startup now aborts server creation instead of surfacing lazily through initErr. Either keep Init separate and let callers invoke it, or update every constructor caller to handle the blocking, fallible behaviour.

It returns false when the shortcut equals the expected one, and it reads substring(3, 5) instead of the grant shortcut at substring(4, 6). WHY: Correct token IDs fail the match, and the check does not validate the grant shortcut as intended. The tests that use expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and similar will fail. WHY: A null rawTokenId is accepted, which produces token IDs ending in "null" and skips the intended validation. FIX: Call `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The encoded prefix is 6 chars (session 0-2, token type 2-4, grant 4-6). Use `items[0].length() == 6 && items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)` and return false when it is NOT equal: `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`.

suggestions.suggestionContent: The grant-shortcut comparison in isAccessTokenId is inverted and off by one. The encoded id is sessionType(2)+tokenType(2)+grant(2), so the grant shortcut is substring(4,6). Use `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`. The current code returns false on a match, so the expected-grant check is wrong.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The message says 'Null rawTokenId not allowed', but the check is on grantType, which is already checked on the line above. rawTokenId is never validated, so a null id passes and the message does not describe what is checked. Change it to Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, "Null rawTokenId not allowed").

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The comment says the grant shortcut is 2 chars starting at the 4th char. The ID format is sessionType(2) + tokenType(2) + grant(2), so the shortcut is at index 4..6, i.e. substring(4,6). The code uses substring(3,5), which spans the last char of the token type and the first char of the grant. The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the shortcut equals the expected one. Fix it to `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;` and correct the comment.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut. The token id format is `ssttgg:uuid`, so the grant shortcut is at indices 4..6, but the code uses substring(3,5). The comparison is also inverted: it returns false when the substring EQUALS the expected shortcut. As a result, the grant-type assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh and the others pass whatever grant is encoded. suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: fetch_error_details pairs error_ids with events.values() using zip. WHY: nodestore.get_multi returns a dict keyed by node_id, and I expect it to omit missing nodes and not preserve request order. Any missing or reordered node shifts the alignment, so errors get the wrong event ID and payload, and the ID pairing is wrong in the logs sent to Seer. HOW: iterate over error_ids and look up events.get(Event.generate_node_id(project_id, id)) for each one.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: the age/timestamp exclusivity checks live in validate_timestamp and validate_age, which DRF runs only when the field is present. WHY: a report with neither age nor timestamp passes validation, even though one of them is required under either spec. Also, the falsy check on initial_data.get('age') or get('timestamp') lets a value of 0 bypass the mutual-exclusion check. HOW: add a validate() method that requires exactly one of the two fields, using `is not None` checks.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: zip(error_ids, events.values()) assumes the get_multi dict preserves the order of error_ids and contains an entry for every id. Neither is guaranteed, so error IDs can be paired with the wrong event data, or shifted when a node is missing. Key the lookup by node id instead: build a dict from error_id to Event.generate_node_id(project_id, error_id), then use events.get(node_id).

suggestions.label: bug

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: join() does `break` once the deadline has passed, so the remaining processes are never terminated. The `process.terminate()` call sits inside the loop after that `break`. WHY: with several processes and a timeout, a slow first process leaves later flusher processes running without terminate(). HOW: do not break; instead skip the wait loop when time is up and always call terminate() for each multiprocessing.Process (or run the terminate step in a separate pass after the wait loop).

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: WHAT: on restart, the old worker is only killed if it is a multiprocessing.Process. A hung threading.Thread (the produce_to_pipe case) cannot be stopped and keeps running while a replacement is started. WHY: two workers then flush the same shards and share the `stopped` and `current_drift` values. Also, `_create_process_for_shards` overwrites `self.buffers[process_index]` with a new SpansBuffer without closing the old one. HOW: signal the old worker to stop through a per-process flag, or only restart workers that are actually dead.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The `time.sleep(0.1)` added here is a no-op because `time.sleep` is monkeypatched to `lambda _: None` at the start of the test. It does not wait for the flusher thread, so the later `(msg,) = messages` assertion can run before the flusher has produced anything. Replace it with a condition-based wait: poll `messages` until it is non-empty with a deadline, using the real sleep captured before patching.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` uses a truthiness test, so an explicit 0 (valid for the int CLI option) is treated as unset and spawns one process per shard. Use an explicit None check, and validate values below 1: `self.max_processes = len(buffer.assigned_shards) if max_processes is None else max_processes`.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The docstring says 'Creates one process per shard', but the constructor now caps processes at min(max_processes, number of shards) and assigns shards round-robin. Several shards can share one process, and the CLI defaults to a single flusher process. Reword it, e.g. 'Creates up to max_processes processes; shards are distributed across them.'

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The wait_produce timer is tagged with the key "shards". The other new metrics (flusher.produce, segment_size_bytes, flusher_unhealthy) use the key "shard". The tag key is inconsistent, so dashboards that group by "shard" will miss this metric. Use "shard" for all of them.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The restart path now kills the old process only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. The processes are created from `mp_context.Process`, where `mp_context` is the spawn context, so they are `SpawnProcess` objects. `SpawnProcess` is a `BaseProcess` subclass, not a subclass of `multiprocessing.context.Process`, so this check is likely always False. The old code called `kill()` unconditionally. A hung process is therefore never killed before a replacement is spawned, which leaks processes that keep flushing the same shards. Use `multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess` in the check, or call `kill()` for anything that is not a `threading.Thread`. The same check in `join()` means `terminate()` is also skipped.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The tag key is inconsistent across metrics. `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `segment_size_bytes` use `tags={"shard": ...}`. `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` uses `tags={"shards": ...}`. Metrics that should be sliced together will not line up. Use one key name, and note the value is a comma-joined list of shards.

suggestions.label: bug
suggestions.suggestionContent: The hung-process kill is guarded by isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process). The flusher processes are SpawnProcess objects, which are not instances of multiprocessing.Process, so the guard is False and kill() is never called. A hung flusher keeps running while _create_process_for_shards starts a second one on the same shards. Both read and flush the same Redis segments, which can cause duplicate production and leaked processes. Check for threading.Thread instead (for example `if not isinstance(process, threading.Thread): process.kill()`), or use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess. The same isinstance check in join() (the terminate call) has the same problem.
